claim: `MUL x, y` followed by `GETQX product` / `GETQX result` is shown as a multiply. MUL is the 16x16 multiply whose 32-bit product lands in Dest (x); GETQX returns a CORDIC result, and with no CORDIC command issued it reads nothing (event 15). The product never reaches `product`. The same file's `cordic_operations` block (:244-249) uses the working pair QMUL/GETQX.
source: p2kb p2kbPasm2Mul ('stores the 32-bit product result into the Dest register'; 'to multiply larger factors, use the CORDIC Solver QMUL'); engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:2054, :3315

claim: short_circuit_evaluation: 'AND/OR stop evaluating when result is known' (example `IF ptr AND ptr.value > 0 ' Won't access ptr.value if ptr is 0`) and performance.evaluation_order 'Left to right with short-circuit'. The v55 operator table defines `&&`/AND and `||`/OR as value operators ('x <> 0 AND y <> 0, returns 0 or -1') and says nothing about skipping the right operand; the v51 interpreter's `bc_logand` is a binary bytecode on two already-evaluated stack values. An example whose point is a guarded dereference drives code, so the claim needs a source or a bench run (this is the only support for the registered S-PENDING-short-circuit-example-untyped-pointer example).
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:489-491; engineering/ingestion/external-inputs/source-code/spin-interpreter/v51/Spin2_interpreter.spin2:1018-1020 (`bc_logand` 'exp && exp (exp AND exp)')

claim: special_features.string_matching: 'Direct string comparison support' -- `CASE command_string` with `"START": ...`. v55 describes CASE as comparing a target value to match values/ranges; nothing documents comparing a string's contents. A five-character quoted literal is rejected in an ordinary expression (`x := "START"` -> Expected end of line, m281), while the same literal is accepted as a CASE match and compiles to a different, 4-byte-larger binary than `"STAR"` (4 chars) or four single-character matches (scratch t/a_casestr 6320 bytes vs t/a3_case4 and t/a2_casechars 6316 bytes) -- so what it does is undocumented. `command_string` here is a pointer; the target is a long.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:738-748 (CASE forms: match value, range, list)

claim: call_cog_registers: `CALL(#fastLoop)` targets code in a DAT `ORG $080`. Nothing loads that code into cog registers ($080), so the CALL jumps to whatever is there. The page text says 'Code loaded at $080 in cog register space' and 'Call PASM code loaded in cog registers'. The source loads first (REGLOAD, or REGEXEC) and then CALLs `#label`.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:840-843 (REGLOAD chunk, then `CALL(#start)`), :820-821

claim: interrupt_coordination: the chunk header is `WORD $110, intEnd-intStart-1` but `temp long 0` and `shared_flag_addr long 0` sit AFTER the `intEnd` label, so they are not part of the chunk REGEXEC loads. pnut-ts listing of the block: INTSTART=$110, INTEND=$117, TEMP=$117, SHARED_FLAG_ADDR=$118 -- the load count is $117-$110-1=6, i.e. $110..$116. The handler's `WRLONG temp, shared_flag_addr` therefore uses a register that was never loaded, and the Spin2 line `LONG[@shared_flag_addr] := @shared_flag` writes only the hub copy. The example compiles and does not do what its explanation says. (The fix is to put the two longs before `intEnd`, as the mathChunk example does with `codeEnd`.)
source: scratch listing g3/t/lst249/main.lst (pnut-ts -l); engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:842-843 ('number of registers (longs) to load, minus 1')

claim: mixed_execution_modes: `COGINIT(COGEXEC, @fastCode, 0)  ' Start in cog mode` -- COGEXEC alone is mode %00_0000 with CogNumber 0, i.e. 'COGEXEC + CogNumber': it (re)starts cog 0 (the cog running this Spin2 program). The starter is COGEXEC_NEW.

claim: 'Register constants in inline assembly': `INA_ADDR = INA` then `rdlong value, ##INA_ADDR  ' Read via constant`. INA_ADDR is a cog-register address; RDLONG reads HUB RAM at that number, not the register. (Reading a register through its address is `reg[INA_ADDR]` in Spin2, as the page's other examples do, or `MOV value, INA` / ALTS-style indirection in PASM.)
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:360 (INA etc. are Cog Registers $1F0..$1FF); the page's own restrictions (:132) 'The constant gets the register address, not the register content'

claim: Spin2 control flow is described as compiled to PASM2: 'CASE_FAST generates jump tables in COG RAM', 'IF generates conditional jump patterns / translates to conditional jumps in PASM2', 'REPEAT generates different PASM2', 'typically 2-4 PASM2 instructions per iteration'. Spin2 methods compile to bytecode run by the interpreter (the KB says so itself); v55 describes CASE_FAST as an 'indexed jump table', not as living in cog RAM. The `pasm_equivalent` sections are illustrations, not what the compiler emits.

claim: parameter_passing: 'Parameters are passed by value (copies made)', note 'Arrays and objects pass references'. Spin2 parameters are longs (or structures up to 15 longs / pointers); an array or object cannot be passed as such -- its address is passed explicitly. The note is unsourced and invites `PUB f(arr)` thinking it receives the array.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:275-277

claim: absolute_address: `@@{variable}` 'Get absolute hub address', examples `@@buffer`, `@@code_start`. `@@x` converts an object-relative offset STORED in DAT data to an address (hub address of this object + x); it is not the general address-of operator (that is `@`). The examples as written read as a synonym of `@`.
